brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Build has 3 piece bases: piece:0,0,0;full (level 0), piece:0,1,0;half-n (level 0), piece:0,1,1;half-n (level 1) — stacked vertically to form a three-cell cabinet column.
Both drawer parts present: drawer:0#0,1#cut at level 0 and drawer:1#0,1#cut at level 1, each seated on the cut face of the half-n bases.

Drawers are installed but neither is in open state. The setDrawerOpen control failed silently twice (no state change after requests open:true, open:true+west:true, and with storeys parameters). This appears to be a configurator bug/limitation — the drawer open animation cannot be triggered in the current session, so the 'pulled open' visual cannot be demonstrated. meshClash is clear and all parts are otherwise valid.

finish.summary: Three-cell cabinet with two drawers is structurally complete and mesh-verified (clear). The second part of the brief — one drawer shown pulled open — is unmet due to a repeated configurator failure to apply the open state to the drawers, despite correct socket installation. LOOSE_BODY warning remains (joint bolts not required for this check).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
